item.stem: A cart moves 6 m to the right and then 2 m to the left along a straight track. Taking leftward as positive, what are the total distance traveled and the net displacement for these two moves?

choices.rationale: Sign-convention reversal: This assigns a positive sign to the net rightward displacement, even though leftward was defined as positive. Fix: Assign a sign to each move using the stated positive direction before adding.
Distance adds the lengths traveled: 6 m + 2 m = 8 m. Displacement adds signed quantities: −6 m + 2 m = −4 m, because rightward is negative.

Distance–displacement confusion: Subtracting the travel lengths incorrectly lets opposite directions cancel in the scalar distance. Distance counts both parts of the trip. Fix: Add all travel lengths without directional signs when calculating distance.

Adding vector magnitudes: Adding both travel lengths and assigning a negative sign treats both moves as rightward. The leftward move must contribute positively to displacement. Fix: Write each displacement with its own sign, then add the signed values.

item.topic_title: Scalars and Vectors in One Dimension
item.stem: A cart moves left along a straight track at a speed of 4 m/s. A student initially defines leftward as positive, then changes the coordinate convention so rightward is positive. The cart’s motion does not change. Under the new convention, what are the cart’s speed and velocity?

choices.rationale: Unchanged-sign error: Keeping the original velocity sign overlooks the changed coordinate convention. Although the motion is unchanged, leftward now corresponds to a negative velocity. Fix: Compare the motion’s direction with the newly defined positive direction before assigning the velocity sign.

Signed-speed error: Applying the leftward negative sign to both quantities treats speed as a vector. Speed has magnitude only and cannot be negative. Fix: Apply the direction sign to velocity, and report speed as its nonnegative magnitude.

Scalar–vector role reversal: Attaching the negative direction sign to speed instead of velocity reverses their roles. Speed cannot be negative, while leftward velocity must be negative under the new convention. Fix: Identify the scalar first, then assign the direction sign only to the vector.
Speed is a scalar, so changing the positive direction does not change its value. Velocity includes direction, so leftward motion has a negative velocity when rightward is positive.

item.stem: An elevator rises vertically at a speed of 3 m/s. An observer first chooses upward as positive, then reverses the axis so downward is positive without any change in the elevator’s motion. Using the revised axis, what are the elevator’s velocity and speed, respectively?

choices.rationale: Unchanged-sign error: This retains the velocity’s original sign despite the reversed axis. Upward motion now points opposite the positive direction and therefore requires a negative velocity. Fix: Match the motion’s direction to the revised axis before choosing the velocity sign.

Signed-speed error: This assigns a directional sign to speed as though it were a vector. Only the velocity is negative; speed is the nonnegative magnitude of velocity. Fix: Remove directional signs from speed and retain them for velocity.
The elevator moves opposite the newly chosen positive direction, so its velocity is −3 m/s. Speed describes magnitude without direction, so it remains 3 m/s.

Scalar–vector role reversal: This places the negative direction sign on speed rather than velocity. Speed cannot be negative, and upward velocity must be negative on the downward-positive axis. Fix: Identify which quantity includes direction, then assign the axis-dependent sign to that quantity.

item.stem: A swimmer travels south along a straight pool lane at a speed of 2 m/s. A coach initially chooses south as positive, but then switches to north as positive without any change in the swimmer’s motion. Which pair describes the swimmer’s speed and velocity using the coach’s revised convention?

choices.rationale: Speed describes magnitude alone, so reversing the coordinate convention leaves it at 2 m/s. The swimmer’s velocity is −2 m/s because south is opposite the newly chosen positive direction.

Unchanged-sign error: Retaining the original positive velocity ignores the reversal of the axis. Southward motion now requires a negative velocity even though the swimmer has not changed motion. Fix: Match the motion’s direction to the revised axis before choosing the velocity sign.

Signed-speed error: Giving both quantities a negative sign incorrectly assigns direction to speed. Only velocity uses the sign to indicate southward motion; speed is a nonnegative magnitude. Fix: Remove direction signs from speed, but retain the appropriate sign on velocity.

Scalar–vector role reversal: Placing the negative sign on speed rather than velocity swaps their roles. Speed cannot be negative, and positive velocity would indicate northward motion under the revised convention. Fix: Classify speed as scalar and velocity as vector before assigning signs.
